St. Macrina the Elder

Macrina, grandmother of Basil · St. The elder Macrina

Period
Early fourth century; exact birth and death dates not supplied here
Region
Pontus; Neocaesarea
Titles / vocation
Righteous · Teacher
Commemoration
January 14

Introduction

The grandmother of Saint Basil the Great, distinct from his sister Saint Macrina the Younger. Her grandson remembered her role in his Christian upbringing.

Read the published life [1]

Death / martyrdom

Exact death date and circumstances are not supplied by these passages

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The GOARCH life of Saint Basil explicitly calls his grandmother St. Macrina a saint and distinguishes her from his elder sister of the same name.

[1] Published Orthodox hagiography · Opening paragraph; family and commemorations

Life and notable events

In Letter 204, Saint Basil says that his grandmother raised him and handed on the teaching of Saint Gregory the Wonderworker. This is direct family testimony to her influence on his faith.

[2] Primary patristic letter · Section 6; grandmother Macrina and Gregory

Death and martyrdom

The family passage does not give her death date or describe an execution. No manner of death is supplied here.

[1] Published Orthodox hagiography · Family passage

Teaching and legacy

Her remembrance concerns the transmission of Christian teaching within a family. Saint Basil appeals to what she taught him as evidence of continuity in his own doctrine.

[2] Primary patristic letter · Section 6

Chronology

  1. Early fourth century

    Her grandson remembers receiving Christian teaching from her as a child.

    [2] Primary patristic letter · Section 6
